summary: Real native inference under enforced address-space (RLIMIT_AS) limits on native ext4 (WSL2). The streamed backend runs a 26 MB GGUF model out-of-core in a 22 MB address space at ~14.5 MB peak RSS, decoupled from model size. The resident backend needs the full model in RAM. The supported model class is narrow (minimal-metadata dense-llama F32/Q8_0/Q4_0), which is the real barrier to arbitrary large-model support, not memory.

source.note: Audit + experiments only; CLI/example built from committed source with no local edits.

environment.note_wsl_not_bare_metal: WSL2 reports ~6.8 GB to Linux; this is NOT a physical 2 GB dual-core machine. Memory results are address-space/RSS bounds, not a hardware feasibility claim.
environment.filesystem: ext4 (native WSL2 disk); models copied off /mnt DrvFs
environment.cgroup_v2_controllers: cpuset cpu io memory hugetlb pids rdma (available)

backends.streamed: Custom CPU forward pass (native/src/streamed.cpp) that streams weights from the authenticated source each pass in bounded 64 KiB range reads; llama.cpp is used only for the tokenizer (vocab_only=1, n_gpu_layers=0). Weights are never fully resident.
backends.resident: Full-model-in-RAM baseline (M1); requires model-size + overhead in memory.

architecture_findings.supported_model_class: general.architecture == 'llama' only; tensor types F32/Q8_0/Q4_0 only; unknown llama.* metadata keys are rejected (native/src/streamed.cpp:71,93,101). Minimal-metadata dense-llama models (stories15M-class). Q4_1, K-quants, and rich-metadata production GGUFs (e.g. Llama-3/Qwen) are NOT supported.
architecture_findings.memory_accounting: --address-space-mb enforces RLIMIT_AS over the WHOLE process (model compute + KV + workspace + read buffers). --max-ram-mb is only a planning estimate, not enforced. The lookahead 4 MiB is a separate read-buffer admission. These are layered, not conflated.
architecture_findings.page_cache_note: Anonymous RSS ~14.5 MB, but cgroup memory.current after a run was ~48.5 MB because the streamed file's page cache is charged to the cgroup. Page cache is reclaimable under pressure; it is not resident anonymous memory.

models.license: fixture derived from llama2.c TinyStories lineage; used as a format-compatibility fixture

models.reason: Q4_1 is not in the streamed decoder's supported set {F32,Q8_0,Q4_0}

coverage_gaps: No model in the 100 MB - 2 GB+ range was tested: no compatible (minimal-metadata dense-llama F32/Q8_0/Q4_0) model of that size is available locally, and downloading large GGUFs was not performed (production GGUFs of that size use K-quants/rich metadata the decoder rejects anyway).

cgroup v2 memory.max enforcement test was skipped: passwordless sudo is unavailable in this WSL2 session. RLIMIT_AS (address-space) was used as the enforced bound instead; cgroup memory.current was still observed via in-process instrumentation.

commands.build: cargo build --release -p llmbridge  (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$HOME/.cache/llmbridge-wsl-target-native; native is a default feature)
commands.inference: /usr/bin/time -v llmbridge chat MODEL --prompt 'Once upon a time' --max-tokens 8 --ctx 64 --threads T --backend {streamed|resident} --address-space-mb AS --metrics

streamed_q8_0_address_space_floor.interpretation: A 26 MB model runs in a 22 MB enforced address space -> weights are NOT resident; out-of-core streaming confirmed.

resident_q8_0.interpretation: Resident backend needs well beyond 48 MB and is not bounded-memory; low-memory execution requires the streamed backend.

thread_variation_streamed_q8_at_24mb.interpretation: Single-core (dual-core target) succeeds; CPU count does not change memory and barely changes wall time for this tiny model/short decode.

full_metrics_streamed_q8_24mb_th2.generated_text_sample: ..., there was a little girl named L

feasibility_matrix.decode: estimated to scale with model_bytes x passes
feasibility_matrix.outcome: Architectural estimate only (no compatible large model available); NOT an experimental result
Verified limitation: decoder rejects the architecture/quant/metadata

correctness_security_preserved.note: No code changed; Phase 2 (deadline/mutation/auth/worker-lifecycle) and Phase 3 (synchronous default) guarantees are untouched. The chat runs above used unsealed source (verified=0); authenticated runs are covered by the Phase 2 evidence.

feasibility_conclusions.bounded_memory_out_of_core: PROVEN for the supported model class: 26 MB model in 22 MB address space, 14.5 MB peak RSS, decoupled from model size.
feasibility_conclusions.two_gb_target: Massively satisfied for the supported class (14.5 MB RSS << 2 GB). The memory floor (~20-22 MB) is a near-constant set by workspace (8 MiB) + tokenizer vocab + KV + 64 KiB read buffer + runtime, independent of model size.
feasibility_conclusions.dual_core: Works (single thread completes; 1/2/4 threads all succeed).
feasibility_conclusions.large_model_barrier: The barrier to large real models is NOT local memory (out-of-core already bounds it) but the decoder's narrow architecture/quant/metadata support. General large-model local inference requires extending the decoder (broader quants/architectures), which is a major, separate engineering effort.
feasibility_conclusions.remote_vs_local: Remote bounded range-read storage (Phase 5) would let the same out-of-core decoder stream a remote model within the same bounded memory; it is a transport, not remote compute.

limitations: WSL2 virtualized, not physical 2 GB/dual-core hardware; RSS/address-space bounds are not a hardware feasibility claim.
Tiny models only (<=26 MB); larger compatible models unavailable; large-size rows in the matrix are architectural estimates, explicitly labeled.
cgroup memory.max enforcement not tested (no passwordless sudo); RLIMIT_AS used as the enforced bound.
Chat runs used unsealed source; authenticated-path correctness is covered separately by Phase 2 evidence.
Decode throughput here is tiny-model/short-decode and not representative of large models.
